standard_prerequisites.name: A closed subscheme without embedded points all of whose components have codimension one in a scheme with unique factorisation domain local rings is an effective Cartier divisor, cited from the same chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns the given closed subscheme into an effective Cartier divisor, hence its ideal sheaf is invertible.

standard_prerequisites.name: On projective space over a unique factorisation domain every invertible sheaf is a twist of the structure sheaf, cited from the same chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies the invertible ideal sheaf with a twist of the structure sheaf.

standard_prerequisites.name: The description of sections of twists of the structure sheaf on projective space over a ring as homogeneous polynomials of the corresponding degree, cited from the cohomology of schemes chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the single homogeneous polynomial cutting out the divisor on each standard open.

core_obligations: Make the ideal invertible: the local rings of projective space over the base are unique factorisation domains, so the given closed subscheme, having no embedded points and only codimension one components, is an effective Cartier divisor and its ideal sheaf is invertible (proof lines 8051-8059).

Identify the ideal sheaf with a twist: invertible sheaves on projective space over a unique factorisation domain are twists of the structure sheaf, so choose an isomorphism from a twist to the ideal sheaf; composing with the inclusion into the structure sheaf gives a nonzero map, which forces the twist's degree to be nonpositive and realizes the divisor as the zero locus of a single homogeneous polynomial F of the corresponding degree (proof lines 8060-8071).

Compute the homogeneous ideal: on each standard open the divisor is cut out by the dehomogenization of F, so a homogeneous polynomial lies in the ideal of the subscheme exactly when each of its dehomogenizations is divisible by that dehomogenization; clearing denominators, suitable powers of each coordinate times the polynomial lie in the principal ideal generated by F (proof lines 8072-8086).

Conclude principality: since the homogeneous coordinate ring is again a unique factorisation domain and the two coordinate powers involved have no common factor, divisibility of the products by F forces F to divide the polynomial, so the homogeneous ideal is generated by F (proof lines 8084-8091).
proof_roadmap: Use the UFD property of the local rings to make the ideal sheaf invertible and the classification of invertible sheaves on projective space to write it as a twist, producing the single equation F (proof lines 8051-8071).
Compute the homogeneous ideal on the standard opens, clear denominators, and apply unique factorisation to get divisibility by F, hence principality (proof lines 8072-8091).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that a closed subscheme of projective space over a Noetherian unique factorisation domain without embedded points and with all components of codimension one is cut out by a single homogeneous polynomial (statement lines 8041-8049). The counted proof is a complete two-stage argument: it first uses the UFD property of the local rings to turn the subscheme into an effective Cartier divisor and the classification of invertible sheaves on projective space to identify its ideal sheaf with a twist, producing a single homogeneous polynomial whose dehomogenizations cut out the divisor on the standard opens; then it computes the homogeneous ideal by clearing denominators on each chart and applies unique factorisation to a pair of coprime coordinate powers to conclude that the polynomial divides every element of the ideal (proof lines 8051-8091). It is H2: both stages are carried out in the counted span, with the cited inputs being standard UFD, divisor and cohomology statements.
